# SPD-045 — Bash hook: >, >>, >|, &> and &>> into a file named by digits or - are skipped as a descriptor

## Brief
separate_redirects drops any operand that is all digits or - for every output operator, but only >& reads such a word as a descriptor or a close. The other operators write a file of that name, so a member writes outside its deliverables (cd docs && echo x > 3) and Spud writes a file past Law 1, with nothing checked. No generated ledger file has such a name, so the harm is bounded to a stray file in a protected directory.

Evidence: Probe (SPD-040, scratchpad, zsh 5.9 -f -o nobareglobqual and bash 3.2): echo x > 3, >> 3, >| 3 and &> 3 created a file named 3 in both shells, &>> 3 in zsh (a syntax error in bash 3.2); > -, >> - and &> - created a file named -; 2> 12 created 12. Only >& 3 and >& - were a descriptor and a close. analyse_command('echo x >3') and ('echo x >-') record redirects []. Fix sketch: skip a digit or - operand only after >& (and keep &-prefixed operands skipped).

## Size, persona and model decision
Batch plan v2, wave 3 with SPD-049, SPD-037 and SPD-035, same engineer on opus. Wholly inside separate_redirects in shell/directories.py: skip a digit or - operand only after >&.

## Outcome
Landed on main as 2f68706 with SPD-049, suite 873 OK. A digit or dash operand is a descriptor only after >&, so echo x > 3 writes a file named 3 and is checked, while >& 3, 2>&1 and >&- stay silent. Its one user-visible cost is SPD-088 at P1: an arithmetic command is read as a redirection, so (( n > 2 )) is now refused as a write to a file named 2. The class existed before for (( a > b )); this widened it to numeric targets, and Bintje pinned the current reading in tests.
